name: S-unit rank/density obstruction to a two-prime Sonine multiplier
statement: For S={inf,2,3} the S-units 2^Z 3^Z have Dirichlet rank 2; their logs n ln2+m ln3 are dense in the one-dimensional scaling flow. The Sonine remainder delta_S23 has log^2 spikes on a dense set, so Lhat_S23>=0 exists only as abstract operator positivity, not a bounded continuous multiplier. A rank-r subgroup of R is discrete iff r<=1.

name: Discrete P_3 pencil is identical to three-place Weil positivity
statement: The pencil D_S + P_3 <= L_S for S={inf,2} is logically identical to W_{inf,2,3}>=0 on pole-free h, because L_S = Arch - P_2 + D_S and D_S cancels. Adding the next prime to the one-prime Sonine inequality gives no unconditional gain past support ln 3.

name: Low-moment corner reduction of D_S<=L_S preserves hardness
statement: For the semilocal pencil D_S<=L_S (S={inf,2}, 2a<=ln3) the global Rayleigh minimiser lies in the k-dimensional low-moment corner, so the corner minimum equals the global margin m(0)=2.8e-3. The finite-constraint reduction does not reduce the problem.

name: Archimedean versus p=2 cancellation ratio as a function of support
statement: On the even Slepian minimiser the ratio residual/P_2 falls monotonically from about 2.3e3 just above a=ln2/2, to 7.52e-5 at a=0.5, to 2.70e-11 at a=ln2 (double-precision floor): about 14 orders of magnitude over the one-prime window.

name: Deligne tensor-power bootstrap: excess m/2 over Z against 1/(2m) over F_q
statement: Over F_q the m-fold self-product gives exponent n/2+1/(2m), tending to the Weil weight. Over Z the Kurokawa tensor zeta has a pole of order m at s=m, excess m/2, giving Re rho<=1 for every m. Finite Euler truncations have no pole and no functional equation. No finite analogue is a partial.

name: Log-cusp out-fraction f_out(rho) -> 1 - 1/rho at S-units
statement: At p=2 the out-fraction of the log cusp at rho=2,4,8 extrapolates (Aitken) to 0.5, 0.75, 0.875 with error below 1.1e-7. For S={inf,2,3} the log^2-cusp fractions approach 1-1/rho from below at every S-unit but do not extrapolate rigorously (mean error 5.9e-2).

name: corr23 continuity reduced to one spectral sum for A_S23
statement: Continuity of the {inf,2,3} correction is reduced to the rho-independent criterion Sum_n |lam_n(A_S23)|^3 / sqrt(1 - lam_n^2) < infinity for the semilocal prolate operator A_S23 = P_1 F_S23 P_1: a spectral gap sup|lam_n|<1 plus a cubic-summable tail.

name: Cubic tail sum of the mixed 2^a 3^b prolate ladder
statement: For the mixed 2^a 3^b ladder Sum_tail |lam|^3 = (C/8)(G2 G3 - 1) = 1.769529 at C=2, a convergent geometric double sum because 2^{-1/2} and 3^{-1/2} are below 1. The ladder tail supremum is s_2 = 0.353553, attained once at u=2; adding the prime 5 leaves it unchanged.

name: No-modulus-1 theorem for A_S23 reduced to the single profile C/v
statement: On the ladder-tail interior the functional equations at p=2 and p=3 (g(v)=2g(2v) and its p=3 analogue) collapse the candidate modulus-1 eigenfunctions from ln2-periodic Zygmund modulations of 1/v to g(v)=C/v. Open: C=0. Indicated by the p=2 top eigenvalue 0.9999731<1, not enclosed.

name: Top semilocal prolate eigenfunction is Zygmund-class, so no analytic-continuation argument
statement: The shortcut band-limited => entire => equal to C/v on a tail interval => pole at 0 forbidden => C=0 fails: the top state of the semilocal prolate operator is fractal (Zygmund), not entire. The residual sits in the cutoff octave (1/2,1), which carries exactly half the cusp.

name: Semilocal {inf,2} prolate spectrum has two eigenvalues near modulus 1
statement: The {inf,2} prolate operator has lam_S(0)=0.9999731 and a second near-modulus-1 eigenvalue lam_S(1)=-0.9927022; the second-largest signed eigenvalue is 0.6202012 (top gap 0.3798). Kato-Temple capture thresholds: adjacent 8.4e-3, bottom twin 1.2e-3.

name: Rayleigh quotients bound the top eigenvalue from the wrong side
statement: For self-adjoint A_S23, R(psi)<=lam_max for every psi, so finite test families give only lower envelopes. Putting lam_max strictly below 1 is the min-principle on I - A_S23 (coercivity over all psi) and needs effective diagonalisation. Kato-Temple thresholds stay at order 1e-3 for every admissible anchor.

name: Kato-Temple certify boundary factorisation
statement: For the 3-level ansatz [1, eps_a, eps_b] on {lam_top, lam_adj, lam_bot} the certify boundary U=1 factors exactly as s0[(t-1)(t-alpha)+(p-1)(p-alpha)eps_a^2+(q-1)(q-alpha)eps_b^2]=0; the per-channel coupling constant is sqrt(3)/2 at every interior anchor.

name: Vanishing-moment sub-family keeps D_S<=L_S past the pole-free crossing
statement: Past the crossing 2a*=1.1316 (= ln3+0.033) the inequality D_S<=L_S fails on general pole-free h, but a sub-family with k>=2 vanishing moments keeps mu_max below 1 (margin 0.392 at 2a=1.16, 0.291 at 2a=1.20). The sub-family certifies nothing about the full cone.

name: Interval-arithmetic port of the analytic legs of the D_S<=L_S certificate
statement: The certificate W(h)=Arch(h)-P_2(h)>=9.04e-4 ||h||^2 on pole-free h in L^2(-a,a), 2a<=ln3, was established in double precision. Two analytic legs are ported to mpmath.iv at precision 200, including the floor constant M_2 in [3.3468106480569850, 3.3468106480569851]. The Galerkin eigenvalue leg remains.

name: Pole-free Weil positivity as the Toeplitz form T_a[sigma_2]
statement: Pole-free Weil positivity on support 2a equals T_a[sigma_2]>=0 on L^2(-a,a), with sigma_2(t)=(t^2+1/4)^2 w_1(t), w_1(t)=2 theta'(t) - sqrt2 ln2 cos(t ln2). T_a[sigma_2] has compact resolvent; a uniform-in-N Galerkin gap is exactly lambda_1(a)>0. Interval-certified for 2a<=0.96.

name: sigma_2 is sign-indefinite, so no de Branges structure forces T_a[sigma_2]>=0
statement: w_1(0)=-6.352, w_1<0 on about [0,3.31] and again on (6.945,10.532). The split bound lambda_min(T[sigma_2^+]) - lambda_max(T[sigma_2^-]) crosses zero at 2a=0.6026<ln2 while the true lambda_1 is far positive. Positivity is a compression (uncertainty-principle) effect; the kernel bound |ghat(w)|^2<=(a/pi)||ghat||^2 is pointwise only.

name: Pole-free subspace as the de Branges space H(E_a S)
statement: PW_a is the de Branges space H(E_a), E_a(z)=e^{-iaz}, with sinc reproducing kernel. With S(z)=z^2+1/4, the map g -> Qg, Q=-d^2/dx^2+1/4, is an isometry of PW_a onto H(E_a S); the pole-free constraint hhat(+-i/2)=0 is membership in that subspace.

name: Galerkin Rayleigh floors of T_a[sigma_2]
statement: Orthogonal Gegenbauer C_n^{13/2} Galerkin (N up to 124, t-converged) gives upper Rayleigh floors lambda_1 about 8.34, 2.16, 0.577 at 2a=1.00, 1.05, ln3; 18.636 at 2a=0.96 (N=36). These are upper bounds by Courant-Fischer; no N-uniform lower bound is established.

name: N-free coercivity T_a[sigma_2]>=c I for 0.96<2a<=ln3
statement: Needed: a lower bound on lambda_1(T_a[sigma_2]) independent of the Galerkin dimension. Rayleigh-Ritz gives only upper bounds; Kato-Temple/Lehmann-Goerisch needs a certified lower bound on lambda_2; the tail-trace bound is vacuous by about 3e15; (N,T) surface fits extract no algebraic rate.

name: Degree-4 certificate atoms capped by 2theta' - sqrt2 ln2
statement: In the Krein cutting-plane certificate the degree-4 tail atoms need min p_4 > -(2 theta'(T) - sqrt2 ln2); the constant 0.98 in -(ln(T/2pi) - 0.98) is exactly sqrt2 ln2, the retained p=2 amplitude, agreeing to 1.2e-5 over T=60..1000.

name: LP conditioning wall of the Krein certificate at 2a between 0.96 and 1.00
statement: The interval-rigorous cutting-plane certificate stops at 2a=0.96: the double-precision LP (HiGHS status 4) fails once eps<=lambda_min. kmax=5 and kmax=6 solves reach near-feasible iterates to about 1.06 in double precision; the interval verification at 2a=1.00 stalls with residual cycling -0.004..-0.052.

name: Super-cubic N-growth of the sigma_2-weighted Krein tail residual
statement: The beyond-T=3200 tail residual of the Galerkin minimiser grows in N with exponent about 3.228, tracking the endpoint-weighted coefficient sum growth q_S (about 3.23), not its rank-1 square 2q_S (about 6.18). Source: sigma_2 ~ t^4 log t tail weight against spherical-Bessel decay of the basis.

name: Three orthogonal gaps between T_a[sigma_2]>=0 and full Weil positivity
statement: Axis I reach (certified 2a<=0.96; LP wall and Rayleigh direction are one obstruction). Axis II pole term: the only assembled bridge D_S<=L_S is obstructed at 2a=ln2. Axis III criterion completeness: Weil positivity quantifies over every support; a per-support certificate is one slice.

name: Pole-term bridge as a codimension-2 positive extension
statement: PW_a = P0 + span{cosh(x/2), x sinh(x/2)}, P0={hhat(+-i/2)=0}. Full Weil positivity from pole-free positivity is a rank-2 Schur-complement problem: the rank-2 pole block is positive but cross terms are indefinite. The Sonine route computes this Schur complement as D_S<=L_S.

name: p=2 resonance blow-up at t_k = 2 pi k/ln2 blocks every local or finite-rank pole bridge past ln2
statement: Un-weighting by (t^2+1/4)^{-1} is nonlocal and breaks the support constraint. The direct Krein positive extension has pole directions concentrated on the same p=2 resonances. E_S o Q grows linearly along t_k=2 pi k/ln2 for every 2a>ln2. The ln2 obstruction is shared by the local, finite-rank and fixed-measure class.

name: Vasyunin Gram matrix of the Nyman-Beurling problem
statement: G_{hk} = gcd(h,k) I(h/g, k/g)/(hk), g=gcd(h,k), with I(a,b) the Vasyunin integral given by cotangent sums V(a,b)=Sum_m (m/b) cot(pi m a/b) plus logarithmic terms. Exact SPD Gram of the dilates rho(1/(hx)); d_N^2 is its Schur complement against chi.

name: Burnol-normalised Nyman-Beurling ratio stays below 1 on N<=10000
statement: ratio(N) = d_N^2 log N / C_Burnol sits at 0.964..0.988 for N in 2600..10000 and does not climb toward the RH asymptote 1 (0.977 at N=1e4). A fluctuating remainder about a plateau near 0.985 fits best; deciding plateau against ratio->1 needs about 1.2 more decades of N.

name: Low-conductor oscillation in the Burnol ratio
statement: The residual of ratio(N) carries a genuine oscillation at frequency w about 4.08 in log N, attributed to a low-conductor band (q=4, 5) of the cotangent table (single-tone R^2 0.685 at q=5, 0.619 at q=4). A gamma_1 alias is ruled out: a gamma_1 tone at w=14.14 is resolved by the grid.

name: lam_min of the Vasyunin Gram decays like N^{-1.918}
statement: lam_min(G_N) follows a power law with p=1.918 (R^2=0.99998; blind N=1e4 prediction within 0.12%). Verified Cholesky certifies lam_min per rung to N about 1.08e5 in double precision; double-double extends this.

name: N-uniform lower bound lam_min(G_N) >= A N^{-p}
statement: Settled as a matrix statement (proved, unrefereed): 1/(64*2^Omega_N*N^2) <= lam_min(G_N) <= (3+log N)/(N-1)^2, Omega_N = max_{n<=N} omega(n), so lam_min(G_N) = N^(-2+o(1)); the lemma lam_min(G_N) >= A N^-p holds for every p > 2, p = 2 open. The same N^-2 law is measured for Davenport-Heilbronn, four Dirichlet characters and two periodic sequences without Euler product, so the bound is a mean-value quantity fixed by the 1/|s|^2 weight; it bounds the size of the optimal coefficients, not the distance d_N, and carries no information on zeros. Earlier text (imp-96613): no analytic N-uniform lower bound was available.
source: imp-96613-route-m-lammin-nuniform-lowerbound-obstruction-assessment; imp-96631; imp-96697; engine lane e1-nb-gram-period-transfer (push/e1-nb-gram-period-transfer/RESULT.md Theorem 1, REFEREE.md)
refereeStatus: proved, unrefereed (author proof in push/e1-nb-gram-period-transfer/RESULT.md Theorem 1; one lane referee pass found no error; no independent second referee; novelty against the literature unchecked)

name: lam_max(G_N) <= I(1,1) H_N
statement: By SPD trace domination lam_max(G_N) <= I(1,1) H_N = 1.2607 log N + O(1), with I(1,1) = log(2 pi) - gamma = 1.2606614. Measured growth is logarithmic with slope 0.3526, entirely an off-diagonal-mass effect. The campaign later proved lam_max(G_N)<=18 (obstruction map P15).

name: Bohr-lift / multiplicative Szego gives only the ceiling log(2pi) - gamma
statement: The Bohr-lift of G_N reproduces the logarithmic shape of lam_max and the ceiling c<=log(2 pi)-gamma but not the measured 0.3526: the lifted symbol carries the zeta pole. No Szego/Grenander limiting distribution or Helson multiplicative-Toeplitz result fixes the edge.

name: gcd factorisation of the Vasyunin Gram Frobenius norm
statement: ||G_N||_F^2 = Sum_{gcd(a,b)=1} I(a,b)^2/(a^2 b^2) Sum_{g<=N/max(a,b)} 1/g^2, so T(N) <= ||G_N||_F^2(interior) <= zeta(2) T(N) with T(N) the coprime-core second moment. Diagonal part I(1,1)^2 zeta(2) = 2.614. Measured R(N)=||G||_F^2/T(N) tends to zeta(2) at rate 1/log N.

name: T(M) = 2 Sum_{b<=M} Q(b)/b^2
statement: With Q(b) = Sum_{a=2,(a,b)=1}^{b-1} I(a,b)^2/a^2, the coprime-core second moment regroups exactly as T(M)=2 Sum_{b<=M} Q(b)/b^2 (checkpoint T(250)=11.757622). An upper asymptotic Int(N)<=s* log N reduces to the uniform lemma Q(b)<=s0* b+O(1).

name: Weighted cotangent second moment Q(b) <= s0* b + O(1)
statement: Open: Q(b) = Sum_{a=2,(a,b)=1}^{b-1} I(a,b)^2/a^2 <= s0* b + O(1) with an absolute s0*. Reduced to the pointwise envelope |I(a,b)| <= K a (1 + log(b/a)) on coprime 2<=a<b via Int_0^1 (1-log x)^2 dx = 5, giving Q(b)<=5K^2 b. Measured slope band s* in 5.66..5.80.

name: Cauchy-Schwarz reduction of the second-moment lower bound to a first moment
statement: Q(b) >= F(b)^2/S(b) with F(b) = Sum_{a=2,(a,b)=1}^{b-1} I(a,b). So F(b)>=kappa phi(b) b gives Int(N)>=(36 kappa^2/pi^2) log N. Measured kappa about 0.696. The campaign proved F(b)>=b phi(b)/2-1 and K=0.6954960511 (obstruction map P15): a mean-value statement, nothing about lam_min, d_N or zeros.

name: Arithmetic part of the Vasyunin first moment
statement: F_arith(b)/(phi(b) b) -> kappa_arith = (3/2)C - 3/8 = (3/4)(log 2pi - gamma) - 3/8 = 0.5704960511. Explicit remainders: L0(b)=Sum_{a in R_b} log a = phi(b)(log b - 1)+E0, L1(b)=Sum a log a = phi(b) b((1/2)log b - 1/4)+E1, |E0|<=2^omega(b)(log b+2), |E1|<=b 2^omega(b)(log b+2).

name: Sum over reduced residues of V(a,b) vanishes
statement: V(b-a,b) = -V(a,b), hence Sum_{a in R_b} V(a,b) = 0 for every b>=2 and Sum_{a=2,(a,b)=1}^{b-1} V(a,b) = -V(1,b), where V(1,b)=Sum_{m=1}^{b-1}(m/b)cot(pi m/b) = -(b/pi) log b + (2C/pi) b - 1/pi + lower order, which is o(phi(b) b).

name: Absolute-value mean of cotangent sums along the inverse line
statement: S(b)=Sum_{a=2,(a,b)=1}^{b-1} V(b,a) = Sum_a c_0(h_a/a), h_a = b^{-1} mod a. Open: A(b)=Sum_a |c_0(h_a/a)| <= c phi(b) b with explicit c<0.5705 (measured about 0.14). The only input is the frequency of small modular inverses b^{-1} mod a: a Kloosterman-type equidistribution statement.

name: Bettin-Conrey reciprocity for c_0(h/k) yields a period function
statement: c_0(h/k) + (k/h) c_0(k/h) is not elementary: it is the Bettin-Conrey / Lewis-Zagier period function (i/2)psi (at (2,5) the value is 0.080325). An Euclidean-descent evaluator of V(a,b) costs O(log q) per pair; the asymptotic R series has a resurgence floor exp(-2 pi/x), cap about 3.3e-6.

name: Residual sign law (-1)^omega(b) of the arithmetic first moment
statement: r(b)=F_arith(b)/(phi(b) b) - kappa_arith satisfies sign r(b) = (-1)^{omega(b)} for 2799 of 2801 b in [200,3000]; on general moduli r(b) b = 0.248 log b + 0.100, with faster convergence on smooth and primorial b.

name: Two-scale spectrum of the Vasyunin Gram
statement: Rank-r power-iteration log-slopes of lam_max follow a logistic in r (half-saturation r0=2.94, width k=0.863, R^2=0.996). The logistic is the exact form of the top-eigenpair weight share w1 lam1^r/Sum w_i lam_i^r in a top-plus-bulk-edge spectrum, width 1/ln(lam1/lam2). The top-eigenvector overlap w1 drifts down over N=1000..6000.

name: Signed-force feasibility LP at near-collision extrema
statement: Strict system g_k.w>0, g_k = sign(Z''(x*)) a(x*) at every near-collision extremum x*, feasible iff 0 is not in conv{ghat_k} (Gordan). Scale-free margin rho(N,T)=dist(0,conv{ghat_k}) by Gilbert min-norm point; rho decreases in the support N.

name: On-line signed-force margin flattens to a positive floor
statement: rho(32,T) fits c + d/ln T with c=0.143, d=2.50 (R^2=0.991) over heights to gamma_200, with decelerating slope; leave-one-out floors stay in [0.121,0.212]. Extensions to gamma_8000 lower the fitted intercept (0.160 -> 0.111 -> 0.071 -> 0.037): the floor is not established.

name: Off-anchor heights sit below the on-line margin law
statement: Over 27 off-anchor heights, 23 lie below the seven-anchor reciprocal-log line (mean -0.0305, worst -0.0608 at T=4506.31). A uniform off-line version of the LP is a statement of Weil-positivity strength; no coefficient set has a universal confining sign on complex pairs.

name: Reach law of the Li-Herglotz-CMV zero detector
statement: Truncation order N needed to detect a zero at height gamma: N_det = 0.364 gamma^1.272 (r^2=0.98); equivalently gamma_det about 2.21 N^0.786. Extrapolated N at the Platt-Trudgian height is of order 1e15. A finite detector restates verified height.

name: Christoffel function of the zero measure nu_a on the circle
statement: Atoms z_rho = (i gamma - a)/(i gamma + a) with mass 4a^2/(a^2+gamma^2), a=20; moments are the Herglotz base sequence and need no zero input. The CMV/Verblunsky Christoffel function lambda_N(theta_k)=1/K_N gives reach N_C = 0.396870 gamma^1.248736; the detector exponent exceeds it by 0.023.

name: Adjacent-box count correlation tends to -1/2 at rate 1/log
statement: For GUE the correlation of counts in adjacent boxes of length L is rho_exact = -1/2 + (log 2)/(2 log(2 pi L)) to leading order. At the Platt-Trudgian height (L=5.9148e6) rho_exact=-0.4817670. Decade ladder to 1e12: deviation falls only 0.0436 -> 0.0188.

name: Empirical lag-1 box anticorrelation of zeta zeros
statement: On Riemann zeros at T=1.5e5 (290 boxes, unfolded edge-to-edge tiling) the adjacent-box correlation of the sd(C-E) statistic is r1=-0.5126; r1 stays in [-0.526,-0.433] for 100 to 1000 zeros per box. GUE proxy: -0.46398. rho_emp is biased toward the rigidity limit relative to GUE.

name: Sine-kernel negative box covariances give variance inflation factor below 1
statement: For the sine process all disjoint-box count covariances are nonpositive with O(1/k^2) lag decay, so the mean over n boxes has VIF<1. Explicit: VIF_291<=0.0752 from rho_1 alone; a certified envelope |DeltaCov_k(L)|<=C(k)/L^2; a third integration by parts gives |R_k(L)|<=(1/(2 pi L))[8/k^3+...]. Conditional on the sine-kernel model.

name: Berry number-variance saturation scale set by the prime 2
statement: L_sat(T) = log(T/2pi)/(2 pi log 2): the box length at which the phase of the shortest periodic orbit (prime 2, period log 2) reaches order 1 and Sigma^2 leaves the GUE curve. Tested on three height cuts of Odlyzko zeros. The sign of |rho_emp+1/2|-|rho_GUE+1/2| changes at L in (60,61).

name: Number-variance offset anchor is a sample maximum
statement: The max offset anchor C0_max=0.333721 caps the number-variance excess at 11 measured heights over about 1.5 decades (6 fitted, 5 held out), and a 25-height grid to T=6.37e5. A -16% excursion at T=1.5e5 saturates it. It is a sample maximum, not a height-uniform cap.

name: Per-window number-variance residual is Gaussian at accessible heights
statement: The per-window (C-E) residual on zeta zeros passes Kolmogorov-Smirnov at six heights (KS 0.030-0.08 below 0.886/sqrt(n)); extreme-value comparison shows Gaussian tails without anomalous spikes; the raw tiling has positive lag-1 correlation, so windows are not exactly independent.

name: Minimal normalised gap of zeta zeros scales near N^{-1/3}
statement: Running minimum g_min(N)/y_N on Odlyzko zeros fits 2.1147 N^{-0.3953}; block-minima per window -0.3818 to -0.3983; Weibull/Gumbel MLE -0.3814 +/- 0.026 (shape 3.92). GUE prediction -1/3 with median envelope 0.8582 N^{-1/3}; the difference is about 1.8 sigma and does not reject GUE.

name: Truncation floor of the Lambda bridge is frozen by verified height
statement: E_trunc = 3.0 T^{-0.4} (kappa*=0.4): about 3.06e-5 at T=3e12. Inverse: H_required(E)=(3.0/E)^{2.5}; floors 1e-5, 1e-6, 1e-7 need H about 4.93e13, 1.56e16, 4.93e18. E(N) decays as N^{-0.47} to N about 3.28e9, then plateaus at E_trunc.

name: No N-decaying truncation tail at fixed verified height
statement: The truncation height H has two parameterisations: fixed H=T_PT gives a floor with no N-dependence; coupling H to N requires zero information above verified height. Neither gives an N-decaying tail, so E(N)->0 is not available unconditionally.

name: Stationarity identity at the peak of the GUE-conditional share
statement: For the share sigma(N)=E_coll/E(N), with a, b the local log-slopes of the component tails: at the peak E_flow/E_trunc = a/b and N_peak/N_flow=(b/a)^{1/(a+b)}, verified across a 0.25x..16x E_trunc sweep to 2e-4. Slope asymptote (1/2,1/2,1). C_C and E_trunc sensitivities combine additively. GUE-conditional diagnostic, not a bound.

name: GUE-conditional collision term dominates the Lambda bridge error
statement: Peak share sigma_max = 0.949 near N about 9.2e5. d sigma_max/d log E_trunc = -0.019 (tightening the unconditional floor raises the conditional share); d sigma_max/d log C_C = +0.048. Landmarks: sigma=0.25 at N about 3.26e10, sigma=0.01 at about 4.62e13, elasticity about -2.09 in E_trunc.

name: E(N)->0 in the Step-4 bridge is gated on an N-uniform C_Lip
statement: Bridge assembly G6 and shock Holder mechanism G6a are closed; rate O((log N/N)^{1/2}) is unconditional; the leading constant C_H reduces to the single factor C_Lip. No N-uniform W_1 Lipschitz constant exists; the field-channel reroute replaces it by a table-certified modulus but leaves G6b-Step1 gap-Lipschitz open.

name: Mirror-descent hypothesis H_desc-mirror(p_req=4.3743) fails at seam height
statement: At the working row (t0=0.1314, y0=0.165) the neutral rigid-lattice Palm mirror count is 2.529 (2-slot) and 3.854 (1-slot); empirical zeta-block minima about 2.67. All are below p_req=4.3743. The 2-slot count grows with slope 0.395 in ln N and reaches p_req at ln N*=18.394.

name: t>0 de Bruijn flow gives no uniform mirror-count lower bound
statement: The well-posed convolution direction is t<0 (multiplier e^{-tau u^2}); the binding direction t>0 has multiplier e^{+t u^2}, unbounded. The flow spreads spacing, the mirror count M decreases in spacing, so M(t)<=M(0)=2.5288<p_req on [0,t0]. Matches obstruction map F1/F2 (flow-blindness).

name: Euler product at t=0 plus flow continuity does not reach t>0
statement: The Euler product exists only at t=0, where the flow-decreasing mirror count is maximal; the uniform bound binds at t=t0 where H_t has no Euler product. Pair-correlation repulsion and gap fluctuations lower M(0). Continuity transports values and derivatives, not multiplicativity.

name: Mollifier reshaping of the pinned prefactor C_F is bounded by 1 + theta
statement: The admissible-mollifier reshaping of the pinned flow prefactor C_F (imp-398) is bounded by the mollified second-moment amplification 1+theta: at most about 1.571 for the longest rigorous mollifier (Conrey theta=4/7). A mollifier changes the flow term by an O(1) factor only.
